heroHeadline: Junta Airstrikes Kill Civilians in Sagaing and Rakhine as NUG Marks Fifth Anniversary of Resistance War — Day 2,046
heroSubtitle: On Day 2,046 (September 9, 2026), junta aircraft killed civilians on two fronts within hours of each other on September 7: gyrocopters and a Mi-35 attack helicopter from the Northwestern Regional Military Command struck a vehicle repair workshop in Tinteinyan Village, Ye-U Township, Sagaing Region, killing 7 and wounding 3 despite no active fighting reported nearby, while a separate jet strike on Thandwe's Ward No. 8 in Rakhine State killed an elderly woman and injured 3 — part of sustained air and naval bombardment of Thandwe and Gwa townships that has continued since September 3. In Tanintharyi Region, a resistance mine attack on a military column near Thayetchaung on September 8 triggered indiscriminate junta artillery, small-arms and drone fire that killed a civilian, while a September 4 drone strike on the Talaw Ta Paw displacement camp in southern Myawaddy Township — sheltering over 4,000 people — killed a child and a woman despite no fighting in the area. On the political track, the National Unity Government marked the fifth anniversary of its 'People's Defensive War' declaration on September 7 with a ceremony attended by 300+ including Acting President Duwa Lashi La and PM Mahn Win Khaing Than, awarding military honors to 1,792 resistance members. These developments continue the same split-screen pattern seen since September 4, when fighting resumed along the Sittwe-Ponnagyun border after a month-long lull and President Min Aung Hlaing landed in Hanoi for a three-day Vietnam state visit; a Cambodia visit follows September 11-12. AAPP's tally puts confirmed deaths since the 2021 coup at 8,335+, with 31,887 people arrested and 22,663 still detained or unverified; ACLED separately confirmed in July that cumulative conflict deaths across all actors have surpassed 100,000. IDPs remain at approximately 5.2 million, with only 26% of the 2025 UN humanitarian appeal funded.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, WFP, ICRC, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group (ICG), Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A), Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), IIMM (UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar), BNI Online (Burma News International), Border Lens, WFP Myanmar, UN Myanmar Country Office, The Diplomat, World Bank, ADB, CNN, Bloomberg, Washington Post, Al Jazeera, AP, EURO-BURMA Office, and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, PDF, TNLA, and SCEF statements.
